sources.title: Quantum error correction below the surface code threshold
sources.abstract: Quantum error correction [1, 2, 3, 4] provides a path to reach practical quantum computing by combining multiple physical qubits into a logical qubit, where the logical error rate is suppressed exponentially as more qubits are added. However, this exponential suppression only occurs if the physical error rate is below a critical threshold. Here, we present two below-threshold surface code memories on our newest generation of superconducting processors, Willow: a distance-7 code, and a distance-5 code integrated with a real-time decoder. The logical error rate of our larger quantum memory is suppressed by a factor of $$\varLambda \mathrm{=2.14}\pm 0.02$$ when increasing the code distance by two, culminating in a 101-qubit distance-7 code with 0.143% ± 0.003% error per cycle of error correction. This logical memory is also beyond break-even, exceeding its best physical qubit’s lifetime by a factor of $$2.4\pm 0.3$$ . Our system maintains below-threshold performance when decoding in real time, achieving an average decoder latency of 63 μs at distance-5 up to a million cycles, with a cycle time of 1.1 μs. We also run repetition codes up to distance-29 and find that logical performance is limited by rare correlated error events occurring approximately once every hour, or $$3$$ $$\times $$ $${10}^{9}$$ cycles. Our results present device performance that, if scaled, could realize the operational requirements of large scale fault-tolerant quantum algorithms.

sources.title: Quantum Error Correction in Quaternionic Hilbert Spaces
sources.abstract: We propose quaternion-based strategies for quantum error correction by extending quantum mechanics into quaternionic Hilbert spaces. Building on the properties of quaternionic quantum states, we define quaternionic analogues of Pauli operators and quantum gates, ensuring inner product preservation and Hilbert space conditions. A simple encoding scheme maps logical qubits into quaternionic systems, introducing natural redundancy and enhanced resilience against noise. We construct a quaternionic extension of the five-qubit code, introducing a framework of 15 syndrome measurements to detect quaternionic errors, including quaternionically rotated error components. Numerical estimates show that the quaternionic five-qubit code achieves a logical error threshold of approximately $p_{th} \approx 0.015$, demonstrating improved performance compared to the standard complex-valued code. These results suggest a new pathway for quantum error correction in high-noise environments, leveraging the richer structure of quaternionic quantum mechanics to improve fault tolerance.

sources.title: Overcoming leakage in quantum error correction
sources.abstract: Abstract The leakage of quantum information out of the two computational states of a qubit into other energy states represents a major challenge for quantum error correction. During the operation of an error-corrected algorithm, leakage builds over time and spreads through multi-qubit interactions. This leads to correlated errors that degrade the exponential suppression of the logical error with scale, thus challenging the feasibility of quantum error correction as a path towards fault-tolerant quantum computation. Here, we demonstrate a distance-3 surface code and distance-21 bit-flip code on a quantum processor for which leakage is removed from all qubits in each cycle. This shortens the lifetime of leakage and curtails its ability to spread and induce correlated errors. We report a tenfold reduction in the steady-state leakage population of the data qubits encoding the logical state and an average leakage population of less than 1 × 10 −3 throughout the entire device. Our leakage removal process efficiently returns the system back to the computational basis. Adding it to a code circuit would prevent leakage from inducing correlated error across cycles. With this demonstration that leakage can be contained, we have resolved a key challenge for practical quantum error correction at scale.

sources.title: Thermodynamic Recycling of Algorithmic Failure Branches: Quantum-Computer Demonstration with Quantum Error Correction
sources.abstract: Thermodynamic trade-off relations dictate fundamental limits on the performance of thermodynamic tasks through costs such as heat dissipation. Here, we propose a framework called thermodynamic recycling to circumvent these limits in quantum processors by exploiting failure branches of quantum algorithms, which are usually discarded. The key component is an athermal bath naturally generated during the resetting of a failure branch. By coupling this bath to a target system prior to relaxation, thermodynamic tasks can be performed beyond conventional thermodynamic limits. We apply this framework to information erasure and derive the reduction in heat dissipation analytically. As a demonstration, we implement our framework on IBM's superconducting quantum processor by combining the Harrow--Hassidim--Lloyd algorithm with three-qubit quantum error correction, thereby reducing the heat dissipated in erasing syndrome information. Despite substantial noise and errors in current hardware, our method achieves erasure with heat dissipation below the Landauer limit. This work establishes an operational connection between quantum computing and quantum thermodynamics for resource-efficient quantum computation.

sources.title: Real-time quantum error correction beyond break-even
Sparse Mamba Decoder for Quantum Error Correction: Efficient Defect-Centric Processing of Surface Code Syndromes
sources.abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is essential for building fault-tolerant quantum computers, requiring decoders that are simultaneously accurate, fast, and scalable. Most state-of-the-art neural decoders achieve high accuracy but process the full dense syndrome array of size $O(d^2 R) $regardless of the actual error rate, where d is the code distance and R is the number of measurement rounds. At physically relevant error rates (p ~ 0.1%), fewer than 5% of syndrome entries contain active detection events -- yet existing decoders process the entire syndrome volume. We introduce the Sparse Mamba Decoder (SMD), a defect-centric neural decoder that processes only the k active detection events using a 13-dimensional feature representation per defect and a Mamba state-space backbone, achieving $O(k)$ complexity. Across depolarizing, uniform circuit-level, SI1000, and Google Sycamore experimental benchmarks, SMD reduces the MWPM logical error rate by up to 49% at $d \le 5$ under SI1000 noise, runs 95-467x faster than the Tesseract near-MLD decoder and 232-463x faster than Belief Matching, and maintains nearly constant latency (24-57 us) across d = 3-9 under uniform circuit-level noise. On the Sycamore experimental dataset, the SMD ensemble matches or slightly surpasses the dense Mamba decoder of Varbanov et al. All results are obtained on commodity NVIDIA GPUs with 7.5-16M parameters, without specialized accelerators.

sources.title: Quantum Error Correction with Quantum Autoencoders
sources.abstract: Active quantum error correction is a central ingredient to achieve robust quantum processors. In this paper we investigate the potential of quantum machine learning for quantum error correction in a quantum memory. Specifically, we demonstrate how quantum neural networks, in the form of quantum autoencoders, can be trained to learn optimal strategies for active detection and correction of errors, including spatially correlated computational errors as well as qubit losses. We highlight that the denoising capabilities of quantum autoencoders are not limited to the protection of specific states but extend to the entire logical codespace. We also show that quantum neural networks can be used to discover new logical encodings that are optimally adapted to the underlying noise. Moreover, we find that, even in the presence of moderate noise in the quantum autoencoders themselves, they may still be successfully used to perform beneficial quantum error correction and thereby extend the lifetime of a logical qubit.

sources.title: Systematic Approach to Hyperbolic Quantum Error Correction Codes
sources.abstract: Quantum error correction codes defined on hyperbolic lattices leverage the unique geometric properties of the hyperbolic space to enhance the performance of quantum error correction. By embedding qubits in hyperbolic lattices, these codes achieve higher encoding rates and lower qubit overhead compared to those defined on conventional Euclidean lattices. Building on recent advances in hyperbolic crystallography, we introduce a unified framework for the systematic construction and scalable benchmarking of CSS quantum error correction codes on hyperbolic lattices. A central component of this framework is the Hyperbolic Cycle Basis algorithm, which employs graph-theoretic methods to efficiently identify all plaquette cycles (parity-check supports) and nontrivial cycles (logical operators). This enables scalable and automated benchmarking of a broad class of CSS codes defined on hyperbolic geometries. We apply this framework to construct and simulate two representative hyperbolic quantum error correction codes (HQECCs), evaluating key performance metrics such as encoding rate, error threshold, and code distance for different sublattices. While HQECCs serve as concrete examples, the framework can be adapted to a wide range of CSS codes, including those with more intricate stabilizer structures such as Floquet codes. This work establishes a foundation for systematic exploration and benchmarking of CSS codes on hyperbolic lattices, paving the way toward practical, high-performance quantum error correction.

sources.title: Quantum Error Correction For Dummies
sources.venue: IEEE International Conference on Quantum Computing and Engineering (QCE)
sources.abstract: In the current Noisy Intermediate Scale Quantum (NISQ) era of quantum computing, qubit technologies are prone to imperfections, giving rise to various errors such as gate errors, decoherence/dephasing, measurement errors, leakage, and crosstalk. These errors present challenges in achieving error-free computation within NISQ devices. A proposed solution to this issue is Quantum Error Correction (QEC), which aims to rectify the corrupted qubit state through a three-step process: (i) detection: identifying the presence of an error, (ii) decoding: pinpointing the location(s) of the affected qubit(s), and (iii) correction: restoring the faulty qubits to their original states. QEC is an expanding field of research that encompasses intricate concepts. In this paper, we aim to provide a comprehensive review of the historical context, current state, and future prospects of Quantum Error Correction, tailored to cater to computer scientists with limited familiarity with quantum physics and its associated mathematical concepts. In this work, we, (a) explain the foundational principles of QEC and explore existing Quantum Error Correction Codes (QECC) designed to correct errors in qubits, (b) explore the practicality of these QECCs with regard to implementation and error correction quality, and (c) highlight the challenges associated with implementing QEC within the context of the current landscape of NISQ computers.

sources.title: Quantum error correction of qudits beyond break-even
sources.abstract: Hilbert space dimension is a key resource for quantum information processing1,2. Not only is a large overall Hilbert space an essential requirement for quantum error correction, but a large local Hilbert space can also be advantageous for realizing gates and algorithms more efficiently3–7. As a result, there has been considerable experimental effort in recent years to develop quantum computing platforms using qudits (d-dimensional quantum systems with d > 2) as the fundamental unit of quantum information8–19. Just as with qubits, quantum error correction of these qudits will be necessary in the long run, but so far, error correction of logical qudits has not been demonstrated experimentally. Here we report the experimental realization of an error-corrected logical qutrit (d = 3) and ququart (d = 4), which was achieved with the Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill bosonic code20. Using a reinforcement learning agent21,22, we optimized the Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill qutrit (ququart) as a ternary (quaternary) quantum memory and achieved beyond break-even error correction with a gain of 1.82 ± 0.03 (1.87 ± 0.03). This work represents a novel way of leveraging the large Hilbert space of a harmonic oscillator to realize hardware-efficient quantum error correction. Quantum error correction of a logical qutrit and ququart were experimentally realized beyond the break-even point with the Gottesman–Kitaev–Preskill bosonic code.

sources.title: Approximate quantum error correction theory of non-isometric codes
sources.abstract: Non-isometric encoding arises in various important contexts in quantum error correction, most notably in the finite-energy, non-ideal codewords inevitable in experimental realizations of continuous-variable codes, and holographic quantum gravity. In this work, we present a general and systematic theory of non-isometric quantum error-correcting codes. In particular, we employ the approximate quantum error correction framework to quantitatively study the fundamental limitations imposed by non-isometric encodings on the accuracy of quantum error correction and implementation of logical operations. We apply our theory to analyze GKP and tiger codes under energy constraints, and discuss the implications to holography.

sources.title: Introduction to quantum error correction and fault tolerance
sources.abstract: These lecture notes from the 2019 Les Houches Summer School on “Quantum Information Machines” are intended to provide an introduction to classical and quantum error correction with bits and qubits, and with continuous variable systems (harmonic oscillators). The focus on the latter will be on practical examples that can be realized today or in the near future with a modular architecture based on superconducting electrical circuits and microwave photons. The goal and vision is “hardware-efficient” quantum error correction that does not require exponentially large hardware overhead in order to achieve practical and useful levels of fault tolerance and circuit depth.

sources.title: Limitations of quantum error correction in noisy intermediatescale quantum (nisq) systems
sources.abstract: Study of the Issue Quantum error correction (QEC) is crucial yet incurs significant qubit overhead costs. The current QEC codes lack sufficient efficiency for near-term devices. The current generation of NISQ devices, which often rely on delicate nanostructured qubit architectures, is prone to noise, decoherence, and gate faults, which severely limit their computing capability and scalability. While traditional quantum error correction codes, such as the surface code, are theoretically resilient, they often require significant qubit overhead and complex management systems that exceed the hardware capabilities of NISQ-era devices. This raises the question of whether new, resource-efficient QEC strategies or hybrid error mitigation approaches can be tailored to the limits of nanostructured NISQ designs. This document examines the constraints of existing quantum error correction (QEC) codes, which are crucial for preserving the fidelity of quantum computations yet require substantial qubit resources. This study examines the shortcomings of current Quantum Error Correction (QEC) codes in relation to Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) devices and explores alternative strategies to create more efficient, low-overhead QEC frameworks appropriate for imminent quantum technologies.

sources.title: A ZX-Calculus Approach for the Construction of Graph Codes
sources.abstract: Quantum Error-Correcting Codes (QECCs) play a crucial role in enhancing the robustness of quantum computing and communication systems against errors. Within the realm of QECCs, stabilizer codes, and specifically graph codes, stand out for their distinct attributes and promising utility in quantum technologies. This study underscores the significance of devising expansive QECCs and adopts the ZX-calculus a graphical language adept at quantum computational reasoning-to depict the encoders of graph codes effectively. Through the integration of ZX-calculus with established encoder frameworks, we present a nuanced approach that leverages this graphical representation to facilitate the construction of large-scale QECCs. Our methodology is rigorously applied to examine the intricacies of concatenated graph codes and the development of holographic codes, thus demonstrating the practicality of our graphical approach in addressing complex quantum error correction challenges. This research contributes to the theoretical understanding of quantum error correction and offers practical tools for its application, providing objective advancements in the field of quantum computing.

sources.title: Approximate symmetries and quantum error correction
sources.abstract: Abstract Quantum error correction (QEC) is a key concept in quantum computation as well as many areas of physics. There are fundamental tensions between continuous symmetries and QEC. One vital situation is unfolded by the Eastin–Knill theorem, which forbids the existence of QEC codes that admit transversal continuous symmetry actions (transformations). Here, we systematically study the competition between continuous symmetries and QEC in a quantitative manner. We first define a series of meaningful measures of approximate symmetries motivated from different perspectives, and then establish a series of trade-off bounds between them and QEC accuracy utilizing multiple different methods. Remarkably, the results allow us to derive general quantitative limitations of transversally implementable logical gates, an important topic in fault-tolerant quantum computation. As concrete examples, we showcase two explicit types of quantum codes, obtained from quantum Reed–Muller codes and thermodynamic codes, respectively, that nearly saturate our bounds. Finally, we discuss several potential applications of our results in physics.

sources.title: Correcting a noisy quantum computer using a quantum computer
sources.abstract: Quantum computers require error correction to achieve universal quantum computing. However, current decoding of quantum error-correcting codes relies on classical computation, which is slower than quantum operations in superconducting qubits. This discrepancy makes the practical implementation of real-time quantum error correction challenging. In this work, we propose a decoding scheme that leverages the operations of the quantum circuit itself. Given a noisy quantum circuit $A$, we train a decoding quantum circuit $B$ using syndrome measurements to identify the logical operators needed to correct errors in circuit $A$. The trained quantum circuit $B$ can be deployed on quantum devices, such as superconducting qubits, to perform real-time decoding and error correction. Our approach is applicable to general quantum codes with multiple logical qubits and operates efficiently under various noise conditions, and the decoding speed matches the speed of the quantum circuits being corrected. We have conducted numerical experiments using surface codes up to distance 7 under circuit-level noise, demonstrating performance on par with the classical minimum-weight perfect matching algorithm. Interestingly, our method reveals that the traditionally classical task of decoding error-correcting codes can be accomplished without classical devices or measurements. This insight paves the way for the development of self-correcting quantum computers.

sources.title: Correction of Non-Linear Adaptive Quantum Error Correction
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: Quantum error correction is a crucial element of quantum computing, enabling the reliable execution of complex computations. Current quantum error correction codes, while effective, often suffer from limitations in their error correction capability. This paper introduces a novel non-linear adaptive quantum error correction algorithm, designed to surpass the limitations of traditional methods. We present a framework that leverages quantum entanglement and instantaneous measurement to dynamically adjust the correction strategy based on the quantum state's fleeting changes, achieving unprecedented accuracy and speed in error correction. The core mechanism hinges on a sophisticated error analysis and feedback loop that optimizes the correction intensity and direction in real-time, mitigating the limitations of fixed algorithms. This work explores the potential for significant advancements in quantum information processing through the implementation of this novel approach.

sources.title: Quantum Topological Correction: A Novel Approach to Robust Quantum Error Correction
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: Quantum topological systems offer a promising platform for quantum computation and communication due to their inherent robustness against local perturbations. However, implementing robust quantum error correction (QEC) on these systems remains a significant challenge. This paper investigates a novel quantum topological correction protocol, leveraging the unique properties of entangled quantum states to achieve high-precision and low-latency error correction within complex topological structures. We propose a quantum topology correction algorithm based on instantaneous information transfer facilitated by entanglement, designed to circumvent limitations imposed by classical error correction techniques. This work demonstrates the potential of this approach to surpass the current state-of-the-art in QEC, particularly for systems exhibiting non-linear topological phases.

sources.title: QuantoTrace: Quantum Error Correction as a Service for Robust Quantum Computing
sources.venue: International Conference on Electrical Engineering and Information Communication Technology
sources.abstract: Quantum computing, despite its vast potential, is impeded by challenges like decoding and system noise, necessitating effective quantum error correction techniques. Our study investigates these techniques, focusing on their practical application. We introduce QuantoTrace, a cloud-based platform offering Error Correction as a Service (ECaaS). It enhances quantum system reliability by detecting, analysing, and rectifying errors, and implements bit-flip error correction compatible with various quantum technologies. Using 3-qubit and 5-qubit models, we demonstrated its efficacy on quantum simulators and IBM quantum hardware. Remarkably, we achieved 100% error correction accuracy on simulators and significant success rates on IBM hardware: 68.95% for error correction and 86.04% for error detection in 5-qubit systems. However, the Quantum Repetition Code (QRC) showed limitations in handling multiple-qubit errors in 5-qubit systems. These findings highlight the potential of QuantoTrace which is based on Software as a Service principles in enhancing quantum computing reliability towards further research needs in quantum error correction, especially for noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices. QuantoTrace aims to simplify quantum error management, making it accessible to a broad user base and facilitating optimized quantum computing strategies.

sources.title: Quantum Adaptive Coding for Quantum Error Correction
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to quantum error correction (QEC) that leverages adaptive coding based on the characteristics of quantum noise. The core claim is that dynamically adjusting the encoding scheme of a QEC code based on real-time noise assessment significantly enhances the reliability of quantum information transmission. The proposed mechanism utilizes quantum feedback control and machine learning techniques to monitor the quantum channel's noise level and subsequently adjust key parameters within the QEC code, such as the redundancy level and the encoding strategy. Traditional QEC codes typically employ fixed encoding schemes, limiting their adaptability to fluctuating noise conditions. This work addresses this limitation by introducing a self-optimizing system capable of responding to dynamic noise profiles, ultimately leading to improved error correction performance. The theoretical framework outlines a generalized adaptive QEC scheme and presents key mathematical formulations for the feedback control and machine learning processes. Further investigation into the convergence properties and performance bounds of the proposed approach is warranted.

sources.title: Quantum Error Correction Adaptive Algorithm
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: Quantum error correction is a critical challenge in quantum computing, requiring sophisticated error mitigation techniques. Traditional error correction methods often rely on fixed strategies, failing to fully exploit the inherent properties of quantum systems. This paper introduces a novel quantum error correction algorithm based on adaptive strategies, designed to dynamically adjust error correction policies based on quantum bit (qubit) characteristics and error probabilities. The core mechanism involves a self-adaptive feedback loop that continuously refines the error correction process, significantly enhancing the overall fidelity of quantum computations. This algorithm has the potential to dramatically improve the performance of quantum systems, addressing a fundamental limitation of existing error correction approaches.

sources.title: Dynamic Topological Quantum Error Correction
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topological quantum error correction protocol leveraging the inherent properties of quantum topology to dynamically adjust quantum error correction parameters. Traditional quantum error correction relies on pre-determined error correction codes, introducing a dependency that limits adaptability. This work proposes a method that utilizes the quantum state's self-adaptive nature to minimize the number of qubits required for error correction, offering a significant advancement in quantum information protection. We detail the core mechanism, focusing on the implementation of a self-adjusting algorithm that responds to changes within the quantum state. This approach addresses a fundamental limitation of existing quantum error correction strategies, paving the way for more efficient and robust quantum systems. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications and future research directions.

sources.title: Quantum Error Correction: A Topological Protocol for Enhanced Quantum Fidelity
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: Quantum information processing is inherently susceptible to noise and errors, posing a significant challenge to the development of robust quantum technologies. Traditional quantum error correction (QEC) methods rely on complex classical information processing, often leading to inefficiencies and limitations in error mitigation. This paper proposes a novel quantum error correction protocol, termed "Topological Quantum Correction," leveraging the unique properties of topological quantum states to achieve superior efficiency and robustness in quantum information processing. We outline the core mechanism, emphasizing the strategic integration of topological structure within the error correction process. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of conventional QEC by directly addressing the inherent vulnerabilities of quantum states, resulting in a more reliable and scalable quantum system. The potential impact of this research lies in advancing the practical application of quantum technologies by providing a fundamentally different approach to error correction.

sources.title: Quantum Geometry Error Correction Computation
sources.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
sources.abstract: This paper explores the potential of leveraging quantum computing's unique properties to develop a novel error correction strategy for quantum computation. Specifically, we propose a quantum geometry error correction approach that transforms geometric calculations into quantum state correction, aiming to mitigate the inherent geometric errors that plague current quantum algorithms. We detail the core mechanisms involved, including the incorporation of quantum entanglement and error-correcting protocols. The paper highlights the significance of this approach for improving the reliability of quantum algorithms, particularly in applications requiring high-precision geometric operations. The investigation begins with a conceptual overview of the challenges associated with geometric error correction and concludes with a discussion of the potential benefits and limitations of this new method.

sources.title: DECODER FOR AN ERROR CORRECTING CODE [WO2026223892A1]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to a computer-implemented method for decoding error syndromes (3) of a quantum error correction code (1) to obtain a recovery set to restore quantum states encoded in the quantum error correction code (1), wherein the error syndromes (3) are results from measurements of the stabilizers (4) of the quantum error correction code (1) executed on a quantum system comprising a plurality of data qubits (5), wherein the quantum error correction code (1) comprises at least two one-lines (6) corresponding to sets of data qubits (5), wherein a tensor product of single-qubit operators acting on each data qubit (5) of a one-line (6) commutes with the stabilizers (4) of the quantum error correction code (1), wherein at least two one-lines (6) have at least one common data qubit (5), the method comprising the following steps: in a rectification step, determining at least one recovery set indicating the set of data qubits (5) on which a recovery operation is to be applied when executed on the quantum system, wherein when the recovery operations are executed on the quantum system a quantum state outside of the code space is transferred to an encoded quantum state in the code space of the quantum error correction code (1); in a post-processing step, for at least one, preferably each, one-line (6) of the quantum error correction code (1) or symmetric differences of one-lines (6) of the quantum error correction code (1), i. determining if the number of data qubits (5) in the intersection of the respective one-line (6) or symmetric difference of one-lines (6) and the recovery set obtained in the rectification step fulfil a predetermined criterion; ii. if the predetermined criterion is not fulfilled, replace the recovery set by the symmetric difference of the one-line (6) or symmetric difference of one-lines (6) and the recovery set obtained in the rectification step; iii. optionally repeating steps i. and ii. until the intersection of all one-lines (6) or symmetric difference of one-lines (6) and the recovery set fulfils the predetermined criterion; outputting the post-processed recovery set.

sources.title: DECISION-TREE DECODERS FOR QUANTUM LOW-DENSITY PARITY-CHECK CODES [US20260340471A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    One or more systems, devices, computer program products and/or computer-implemented methods of use provided herein relate to decision tree decoding for quantum low-density parity check codes. For example, a system can comprise a memory that can store computer executable components and a processor that can execute the computer executable components stored in the memory. The computer executable components can comprise a graph construction component that can construct a decision tree given a syndrome measurement of a quantum processor on a decoding graph of a quantum error correction code. The computer executable components can further comprise an exploration component that can explore the decision tree by incrementally adding a fault to a fault set to construct a correction for the syndrome measurement.

sources.title: SCALABLE TRAINING OF IMPROVED DETECTOR ERROR MODELS FOR DECODERS OF QUANTUM ERROR CORRECTION CODES [WO2026217118A2]
sources.abstract: One example aspect of the present disclosure is directed to a method for operating a quantum computing system (QCS). The QCS has a set of qubits. The method includes accessing detection event data that includes stabilizers measurements for a set of stabilizers of a quantum error correction (QEC) code implemented, via. the QCS, on the set of qubits. A trained detector error model (DEM) for a decoder of the QEC code is generated. The trained detector DEM is generated by iteratively updating a set of candidate DEMs based on the detection event data and an optimization algorithm that includes an objective. A. quantum algorithm is performed, via. the QCS, based on the QEC code with the decoder configured to use the DEM.

sources.title: A METHOD FOR PROVIDING MULTIPLE ROUNDS OF ERROR CORRECTIONS FOR A QUANTUM ERROR CORRECTION CODE [EP4818990A1]
sources.abstract:
[0001]    The invention concerns a method for providing rounds of error corrections for a quantum error correction code comprising the following steps:
- initializing a quantum register with N data qubits and a number R of sets of K ancilla qubits,
- encoding logical information on the N data qubits,
- performing R cycles of operations on the quantum register, each cycle of operations comprising entangling gates between part of the N data qubits with part of a distinct set of K ancilla qubits, and
- obtaining measurements from the N data qubits and from each of the R sets, each measurement being the result of a quantum projection operation applied on the considered qubit and of the readout of the quantum projection, the measurements obtained from the R sets enabling carrying out R rounds of error corrections on the measurements obtained from the N data qubits.

sources.title: Quantum Error Correction Decoding via Block-and-Cycle Feasibility Checking [US20260300797A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    Systems/techniques that facilitate quantum error correction decoding via block-and-cycle feasibility checking are provided. In various embodiments, a system can measure a syndrome measurement associated with a quantum error correction circuit and a parity check matrix. In various aspects, the system can identify a logical action caused by an error afflicting the quantum error correction circuit, based on performing block-and-cycle feasibility checking on a first linear system derived from the syndrome measurement and from the parity check matrix. In various instances, the system can correct the error, based on applying an inverse of the logical action to the quantum error correction circuit.

sources.title: METHOD FOR PERFORMING QUANTUM ERROR CORRECTION [US20260300796A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A method for constructing a quantum error correction code based on weight reduced classical code is described herein. When the weight of a row r of the classical code check matrix is above a weight threshold x, the row is replaced with a matrix M comprising a first sub-matrix and a second sub-matrix. The first sub-matrix is constructed such that the i-th column of the first sub-matrix has a weight equal to the i-th element of row r. Each column of the second submatrix having a non-zero even-numbered weight. Each row of the second sub-matrix having a weight of less than or equal to (x−w<1>), w<1 >being the weight of a corresponding row of the first sub-matrix. Then zeros are appended to the end of each row of check matrix besides row r, producing a weight reduced check matrix, from which a quantum error correcting code may be constructed.

sources.title: MODELS FOR DETERMINING LOGICAL ERROR RATES FOR QUANTUM ERROR CORRECTION CODES OPERATING ON QUBIT ARRAYS WITH NON-UNIFORM PHYSICAL ERROR RATES [CA3323268A1]
sources.abstract: One example aspect of the present disclosure is directed to a method for operating a quantum computing system (QCS). The method includes accessing a set of physical error rates. Each physical error rate of the set of physical error rates corresponds to a physical error rate of a qubit of the set of qubits. The set of physical error rates is non-uniform. A predicted logical error rate for a quantum error correction (QEC) code is determined. The QEC code corresponds to the set of qubits. Determining the predicted logical error rate is based on the set of physical error rates and a logical error rate model for the QEC code. The QCS is operated in accordance with the predicted logical error rate for the QEC code.

sources.title: QUANTUM COMPUTING SYSTEM [WO2026190444A1]
sources.abstract: Disclosed herein is a computer-implemented method for performing syndrome extraction in a quantum error correction procedure in quantum computing hardware. The quantum error correction procedure initially encodes one or more logical quantum states in a plurality of data qubits of the quantum computing hardware. The syndrome extraction comprises a plurality of stabilisers each initially associated with a respective auxiliary qubit of the quantum computing hardware. The method comprises applying entangling gates on the plurality of data qubits and the plurality of auxiliary qubits according to a uniform stabiliser measurement schedule, wherein each entangling gate is in a same equivalence class as an iSWAP gate, wherein each entangling gate is configured to act on a data qubit and an auxiliary qubit. The method further comprises measuring the respective auxiliary qubit associated with each stabiliser following completion of the uniform stabiliser measurement schedule.

sources.title: QUANTUM COMPUTING SYSTEM [WO2026190445A1]
sources.abstract: Disclosed is a computer-implemented method for performing syndrome extraction in a quantum error correction (QEC) procedure in quantum computing hardware with degree-four connectivity. The QEC procedure initially encodes one or more logical quantum states in a plurality of data qubits of the quantum computing hardware. The syndrome extraction comprises a plurality of stabilisers each initially associated with a respective auxiliary qubit of the quantum computing hardware, at least one stabiliser having a weight great than four. The method comprises applying entangling gates on the plurality of data qubits and the plurality of auxiliary qubits according to a non-uniform stabiliser measurement schedule, each entangling gate is in a same equivalence class as an iSWAP gate, each entangling gate is configured to act on a data qubit and an auxiliary qubit. The method further comprises measuring the respective auxiliary qubit associated with each stabiliser following completion of the uniform stabiliser measurement schedule.

sources.title: CLIFFORD-IN-MEMORY MODULAR FAULT-TOLERANT QUANTUM COMPUTING ARCHITECTURE [US20260268200A1]
sources.abstract: One or more systems, devices, computer program products and/or computer-implemented methods of use provided herein relate to modular fault-tolerant quantum computing. For example, a system can comprise a memory that can store computer executable components and a processor that can execute the computer executable components stored in the memory. The computer executable components can comprise an operation component that performs, on a quantum processor, stabilizer operations on logical qubits encoded in a quantum error correction code. The computer executable components can further comprise an execution component that performs, on the quantum processor, universal quantum operations on the logical qubits using the stabilizer operations, wherein the stabilizer operations consume magic state.

sources.title: CLIFFORD-IN-MEMORY MODULAR FAULT-TOLERANT QUANTUM COMPUTING ARCHITECTURE [WO2026185268A1]
sources.abstract: One or more systems, devices, computer program products and/or computer-implemented methods of use provided herein relate to modular fault-tolerant quantum computing. For example, a system can comprise a memory that can store computer executable components and a processor that can execute the computer executable components stored in the memory. sources.title: METHOD AND QUANTUM HARDWARE FOR QUANTUM ERROR CORRECTION [EP4804090A1]
QUBIT ARRAY, QUANTUM COMPUTER, AND QUANTUM ERROR DETECTION METHOD [US20260289380A1]
sources.abstract: There is provided a qubit array that realizes computations between a plurality of logical qubits implementing a quantum error correction code while securing space for the wiring and elements required for qubit control. The qubit array includes: a first quantum dot row in which a plurality of data qubits or a plurality of syndrome qubits are arranged so as to be movable; and a second quantum dot row in which the plurality of data qubits or the plurality of syndrome qubits are fixed. A double ring including an outer ring and an inner ring is formed by arranging a pair of the first quantum dot row and the second quantum dot row in a loop shape.

sources.title: QUANTUM ERROR CORRECTION WITH INDEPENDENT DECODING WINDOWS [WO2026180792A1]
sources.abstract: A quantum error correction method and quantum computing system are disclosed. The quantum computing system receives syndrome data and sets defect states of nodes in a decoding hypergraph according to defects identified in the syndrome data. The quantum computing system determines a plurality of decoding windows associated with logical observable subsets of a logical observable and independently decodes the decoding windows to determine partial corrections. The partial corrections are then combined by the quantum computing system to determine an aggregate correction for an error state of quantum devices in the quantum computing system.

sources.title: CHARACTERIZATION USING NON-CONVENTIONAL MODALITIES OF COMPUTATION [US20260260153A1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    One or more properties of a quantum error correction protocol are specified in a formal language using a theorem prover. A quantum error correction protocol and a formal proof certificate are synthesized, the formal proof certificate being a machine-checkable proof that the quantum error correction protocol satisfies the one or more properties. The quantum error correction protocol is compiled into a quantum circuit with the formal proof certificate embedded in the quantum circuit. The quantum circuit is deployed onto quantum computing hardware.

sources.title: Parallel decoding method and device for distributed quantum error correction of multiple measurement chips [CN122656018A]
authors: BEIJING QUANTUM INFORMATION SCIENCE RESEARCH INST
sources.organization: BEIJING QUANTUM INFORMATION SCIENCE RESEARCH INST
sources.abstract: The invention discloses a parallel decoding method and device for distributed quantum error correction of multiple measurement chips, and relates to the technical field of quantum error correction. The method comprises the following steps: dividing a Tanner graph into a cross-chip boundary sub-graph and a plurality of chip local sub-graphs according to an obtained check matrix of a quantum error correction code, channel mapping, communication constraints among a plurality of measurement chips and the Tanner graph corresponding to the check matrix; determining a local syndrome; performing parallel local decoding on each chip local sub-graph based on a local syndrome to obtain local candidate correction, a local residual summary and boundary state information; determining a boundary message packet according to the boundary state information; exchanging boundary message packets between adjacent measurement chips; based on the boundary message packet, executing a preset number of rounds of boundary fusion on the cross-chip boundary sub-graph to obtain a fusion correction result; and performing global consistency verification according to the fusion correction result and the local residual abstract to obtain a final correction result.

sources.title: Quantum Error Correction Using Mid-Cycle Single-Qubit Gauge Operators [US20260252941A1]
sources.abstract: A method can include measuring, at one or more mid-cycle states of a quantum error correction code executing on a quantum computing system, one or more mid-cycle gauge operators and one or more mid-cycle stabilizers. In the method, the one or more mid-cycle gauge operators comprise one or more single-qubit mid-cycle gauge operators. The method can include performing, based at least in part on a result of the measuring, a quantum error correction operation.

sources.title: Error correction method and device of NV color center Isin machine, electronic equipment and readable medium [CN122635587A]
authors: BEIJING BOSE QUANTUM TECH CO LTD
sources.organization: BEIJING BOSE QUANTUM TECH CO LTD
sources.abstract: The invention relates to an error correction method and device of an NV color center Isin machine, electronic equipment and a readable medium. The method comprises the following steps: mapping an electronic spin state of an NV color center to a plurality of nuclear spins for redundant coding; obtaining a read-out result of the plurality of nuclear spins; determining a corrected spin state through a majority voting rule based on the plurality of read results; and according to the statistical deviation in the error correction process, the control pulse parameters are dynamically adjusted. Nuclear spin naturally existing around the NV color center is used as a redundant carrier, overturning errors in the reading process can be corrected without additional hardware resources, the overall fidelity of the Isin machine is remarkably improved, accumulation of systematic errors is restrained by dynamically adjusting and controlling pulse parameters, and the reading accuracy of the Isin machine is improved. The problems that the fidelity is reduced due to error accumulation in the measurement feedback iteration process of the NV color center Isin machine and the general quantum error correction resource overhead is large are solved.

sources.title: Quantum Error Correction Apparatus and Method Thereof Using a Cross-Grid Structure [KR103008840B1]
Quantum error correction decoding method and device, computer equipment, storage medium and computer program product [CN122616762A]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of quantum computing, in particular to a quantum error correction decoding method and device, computer equipment, a storage medium and a computer program product, and the method comprises the steps: obtaining verification sub-data generated in a quantum error correction process, carrying out the preprocessing of the verification sub-data, coding the data obtained after preprocessing to an optical carrier, and carrying out the decoding of the optical carrier. Generating a light field carrying syndrome information; enabling the light field to pass through a diffraction layer along the light path direction, performing phase and/or amplitude modulation on the light field by the diffraction layer, and performing optical calculation by utilizing a diffraction effect; and receiving the output light field processed by the diffraction layer, detecting the intensity distribution of the output light field, and determining and outputting a decoding result according to the intensity distribution. The all-optical frame is adopted for syndrome classification, the decoding process is executed at the light velocity, power consumption is extremely low, the strict requirement of a high-performance quantum architecture for the decoding speed can be met, and the backlog problem is effectively avoided.

sources.title: A computer system comprising a quantum processing unit and a classical computing device [GB2704277A]
sources.abstract: A computer system comprises a quantum processing unit comprising quantum bit units and cryogenic readout circuits to output a readout signal from a corresponding quantum bit unit. The computer system further comprises: for each group of readout circuits 40, a cryogenic transmitter module 46 configured to serialise, via serializer 60, the readout signals into a stream of digital signals; a communication channel 50 configured to transmit the stream of digital signals; a receiver module configured to deserialize the stream; and a classical computing device configured to store deserialized data in a memory. The transmitter may comprise a line code encoder 58 (e.g. for iManchester code or 8b/10b code). Avoids need to rely on frequency multiplexing by implementing a novel data communications protocol. Scalability of the readout infrastructure of a cryogenic quantum computing system is improved, in terms of thermal load on the mixing chamber due to cable numbers, and the amount of readout information per unit time. The protocol is used for quantum error correction techniques. [Fig 6]

sources.title: Quantum error correction method, device and equipment, storage medium and program product [CN122549621A]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to the technical field of computers, in particular to a quantum error correction method, device and equipment, a storage medium and a program product. The quantum error correction method comprises the steps that periodic measurement is conducted on first structures and second structures in a quantum system, the second structures comprise a plurality of first structures, and each period in the periodic measurement comprises multiple times of measurement on the first structures and at least one time of measurement on the second structures; determining a measurement result of a stabilizer in the quantum system according to the measurement results of the first structure and the second structure, the stabilizer representing an invariant in the quantum system; and performing error correction on the quantum system according to the measurement result of the stabilizer.

sources.title: Broadcast system and method for event distribution [GB2704240A]
sources.abstract: A messaging system for a distributed quantum system (e.g. a quantum control system and/or a quantum error correction unit). The system has a plurality of real-time units (e.g. decoders, sequencers or quantum control units) 201a-201h, 203a-203d, 205a-205b, 207 each real-time unit being communicatively couplable to a respective proper subset of a plurality of quantum devices (e.g. qubits). The plurality of real-time units are assigned into groups, each group being addressable as a single group. Each of the real time units is configured to receive messages sent to the group they are assigned to and to determine whether to ignore or process received messages based on an identifier included in the message. The groups may be assigned so that at least one group comprises quantum devices that comprises physical qubits corresponding to the same logical qubit. The groups may be arranged in a hierarchical structure and the identifiers included in the messages may indicate the hierarchical level to which the message is sent. Figure 2

sources.title: Scalable quantum error correction architecture using dual-function Transmon couplers in a fluxonium qubit array [US12699915B1]
sources.abstract: [0000]    A system for quantum error correction can store quantum information while supporting controlled interactions for syndrome measurements. The system includes a plurality of fluxonium qubits arranged as data qubits. The system further includes a plurality of transmon qubits arranged as ancilla qubits, each positioned between a respective first fluxonium qubit and a respective second fluxonium qubit. The system further includes, for each transmon qubit, a tunable coupling element connected between the first and second fluxonium qubits. The system further includes a coupling control circuit connected to each tunable coupling element, the coupling control circuit configured to set a desired coupling strength during active operations and to increase the impedance state during idle periods to isolate the fluxonium qubits from residual interactions, thereby improving coherence times and reducing error rates in quantum computation.

sources.title: Efficient quantum key generation method based on entangled state and stable subcode [CN122513093A]
sources.abstract: The invention relates to an entangled state and stable subcode-based efficient quantum key generation method, which comprises the following steps of: constructing a plurality of groups of original GHZ entangled states, distributing a first particle sequence and a second particle sequence to a sender, and distributing a third particle sequence to a receiver; respectively applying a first unitary operation and a second unitary operation to each particle in the first particle sequence and the second particle sequence, and forming a distinguishable GHZ entanglement state with the third particle sequence; preparing a plurality of verification particles to obtain verification sequences and corresponding preparation bases, and pairing the verification sequences and the preparation bases to form a plurality of composite particle groups; each composite particle group is coded through a quantum error correction code to obtain a composite quantum system; and decoding the composite quantum system through the quantum error correction code, and retaining the effective particle group to perform GHZ-based measurement to generate a final key. The method can improve the key generation efficiency, has the single-bit error correction capability, is high in noise resistance, and is simple and efficient in eavesdropping detection.
